claims.source_quote_ar: الشَّيْطانُ خبر ذلكم، بمعنى: إنما ذلك المثبط هو الشيطان.
claims.claim_ar: أُستعملت كلمة «الشَّيْطانُ» خبراً محدّداً للمثبط — تصوير الشيطان باعتباره سبب الضلال بمعنى مجازي (مجاز/استعارة معنوية).
claims.claim_en: The word 'الشَّيْطانُ' functions as the predicate identifying 'the demotivator' — portraying Satan as the cause of misguidance in a figurative/majaz sense.
claims.needs_review_reason: Some commentators might treat this as literal identification or kināyah rather than majaz; classification between majaz and kināyah is interpretive and may vary.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Identifies and externalizes the cause of the person's deviation, strengthening the moral attribution of blame to Satan and making the cause more concrete for the listener/reader.

claims.source_quote_ar: ويخوّف أولياءه: جملة مستأنفة بيان لشيطنته.
claims.claim_ar: وجود «جملة مستأنفة» حول لفظة «الشيطان»؛ لفظةُ الشيطان تُعرض كوقفة مستأنفة لإبرازها وتأكيد صلتها بالعمل (التفات/التوكيد).
claims.claim_en: The commentator notes a 'resumed clause' around the term 'الشَّيْطانُ'; presenting 'الشَّيْطانُ' as a resumed/interrupted clause serves to spotlight and emphasize the role of Satan (an instance of iltifat/turning for emphasis).
claims.needs_review_reason: The identification of this pattern as iltifat depends on reading/punctuation and could alternatively be read as simple apposition or syntactic completion; requires cross-check with other tafsir/grammatical analyses.
claims.rhetorical_effect: Creates a sudden shift that draws attention to the agent of misguidance, increasing emphasis and emotional impact.

warnings: Source chunks provided are from Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf). The developer instructions requested al-Jurjānī, al-Sakkākī, al-Baqillānī, al-Suyūṭī and tafsir-balagha sections; those specific authors' chunks were not provided. Claims are therefore drawn only from the supplied Zamakhshari excerpts.

Some classifications (e.g., majaz vs. kināyah, or iltifat vs. simple apposition) are interpretive; confidence marked 'medium' where alternative readings are plausible. Review against additional tafsir/balāgha sources is recommended.
